subject: Archaeology
title: The Last Day of Pompeii
description: A 60-second lesson on The Last Day of Pompeii.

hook.text: On August 24, 79 CE, Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii under 20 feet of volcanic ash in less than 24 hours.

buildup.text: Pliny the Younger watched from across the bay and wrote a detailed account — the first eyewitness report of an eruption.

discovery.text: Most victims died not from lava but from pyroclastic surges — superheated gas clouds traveling at 450 miles per hour.

twist.text: Many residents ignored early tremors and stayed home. Romans did not understand volcanoes as natural phenomena.

climax.text: About 2,000 of Pompeii's 11,000 residents died. Most had time to flee but chose not to leave their belongings.

punchline.text: They stayed for their possessions. The volcano took everything anyway.

quiz.question: What killed most victims at Pompeii?
options: Lava flows that engulfed the city streets
Pyroclastic surges — superheated gas clouds at 450 mph
Collapsing buildings from the weight of falling ash
